title: Personal Checking: Identifying the Debit That Opened a Negative Episode
content:
## Which extended overdraft fee

The error review of Personal Checking extended overdraft fees concerns the extended overdraft fee most recently posted to the account. Earlier extended overdraft fees are judged under the general Personal Checking fee refund rules.

## Dating the episode

An extended overdraft fee is posted the tier's trigger period, in calendar days, after the date on which the negative episode began. The fee's own posting date therefore fixes the day the episode opened: that posting date less the trigger period.

## Finding the debit that opened it

The opening debit is traced through the overdraft item fee most recently posted to the account:

- If the gap between that overdraft item fee's posting date and the extended overdraft fee's posting date is exactly the trigger period in calendar days, the overdraft item fee was booked on the opening day of the episode, and the debit it names as its source item is the debit that opened the episode.
- If it posted on any other day, or no overdraft item fee exists, the opening debit is not identified, and no finding can be based on the opening debit.

## Date check (hypothetical trigger period of 5 days)

| Extended overdraft fee posted | Latest overdraft item fee posted | Days between | Opening debit identified? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 15 May 2026 | 10 May 2026 | 5 | yes — the source item of the 10 May fee |
| 15 May 2026 | 11 May 2026 | 4 | no |
| 15 May 2026 | 2 May 2026 | 13 | no |
| 15 May 2026 | none | — | no |

The count of days between is a plain calendar-day difference between the two posting dates.
